correctness.rationale: The four-state forbidden-factor automaton is exact. Universal quantification over all queried assignments becomes deterministic antichain updating, with 14 states reproduced independently. The transfer matrix proves the rational generating function; exact symbolic elimination reproduces the numerator and denominator. A 14-value potential satisfies every weighted transition inequality and proves the infinite upper bound. Accepted supports 11(001)^k followed by 0, 1 or 2 zeros attain the dimension; n=0 and n=1 are treated separately. Full trace enumeration n<=12 and 28 coefficient checks corroborate, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: Full text of the closest indexed forbidden-triple shattering result was read; it forbids 000 and 111, obtains a structurally different support language and a dimension with slope 1/2. A related earlier 000/101 result has a different forbidden-pair orbit and rational series. The closest general primary paper by Johnson studies the translates of a single infinite word, not full finite-language coordinate projections. Exact claim comparison and indexed published-finding corpus searches found no implication covering the 000/011 family. Residual unindexed historical priority remains possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible historical publication may derive an equivalent 000/011 all-order shattering formula.
The two arXiv primary papers were inspected at abstract/excerpt scope rather than comprehensively page-by-page; the most directly comparable 000/111 shattering paper was read fully.

value.rationale: The two forbidden factors encode a natural conditional alternation rule: whenever a zero occurs, its next two bits differ. The theorem supplies a complete infinite family of shattered-support counts and exact regular-language recognition, with a sharp one-third coordinate-learning density unlike the half-density of the nearby 000/111 system. The finite 14-state certificate makes this structural result reproducible and mathematically motivated; the claim is not a general arbitrary-pair classification.
